close_reason: Replaced from_value(val.clone()) -> Metadata with UniquenessKey::from_stored(&val) helper at memory.rs:931 (using pre-existing helper at memory.rs:312). Net 1 fewer deserialize + 1 fewer Value::clone per create. The full echo path (O::deserialize(&val) at line 957) is unchanged — it remains the unavoidable typed-O construction. cargo clippy --tests -- -D warnings clean; cargo test --all-features clean (21 unit + 21 integration tests pass).
description:
memory.rs:696-697: val = serde_json::to_value(&obj). memory.rs:728-731: stored_obj: O = O::deserialize(&val). The intermediate steps are uniqueness checking (only when O::TYPE_NAME == Metadata::TYPE_NAME) and injecting the server-assigned id at memory.rs:728.

For a typical create: serialize O, parse as Metadata, compute uniqueness key, then deserialize a slightly-modified val back to O. That is serialize+parse+inject+deserialize for one create. Net: every create pays 2x serde round-trips on the same JSON value.

Impact: small in absolute terms (Annotation is small JSON), but happens on every create. For a reference impl this is fine; for a teaching impl, the wasteful round-trip would be copied into a real backend.

Fix direction: instead of round-tripping via serde, mutate val directly to inject id, then keep val as the stored value AND construct stored_obj from val. The double serde is structurally unnecessary — Metadata implements both Serialize and Deserialize directly.
title: MemoryBackend.create_object serializes obj to JSON then immediately deserializes the same JSON back to O — pointless round-trip on every create
